key_insight: AEAPTMS passivation makes mixed-halide perovskite surfaces electronically more uniform and faster to reach a stable photoresponse, indicating reduced interfacial disorder and grain-boundary barriers.
engineering_relevance: This suggests amino-silane surface treatment can improve perovskite solar cell performance by lowering photovoltage losses and stabilizing the carrier landscape at the nanoscale.
method: Measured dark contact potential difference (CPD) and illuminated surface photovoltage (SPV)
Separated grain-boundary and grain-interior potential contributions; used wavelength-dependent SPV
evidence_signal: Passivation narrowed dark CPD distribution from about 45.7 to 14.6 mV, increased steady-state SPV from about 345 to 417 mV, and reduced the stabilization time constant from about 840 to 470 s.
watch_item: Results come from thin-film nanoscale measurements, so translating the observed electronic improvements to full-device stability and efficiency still needs validation.
paper_title: Understanding surface potential dynamics of passivated perovskites via Kelvin Probe Force Microscopy
